Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Evidence for digital revenue collection (taxes/fees) was not collected from an authoritative Moroccan revenue authority source in this run; searches focused on payments ecosystem and found references to intent rather than documented implementation.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Escalated from fast-path Unknown after a single light-check search surfaced authoritative primary sources. Morocco's customs authority (ADII) operates BADR, its electronic customs clearance system, which explicitly enables 'paiement électronique des droits et taxes' (electronic payment of customs duties and taxes) per the official douane.gov.ma page. Separately, the Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) operates the SIMPL portal (tax.gov.ma), through which electronic filing and payment of Corporate Tax (CIT), VAT, and Personal Income Tax (PIT) has been mandatory for all taxpayers since 1 January 2017 (Article 155, General Tax Code), confirmed via the DGI's own site and a detailed secondary explainer. Both major state taxes and customs duties are payable digitally, so the score is revised from 0/Unknown to 3/Yes (Comprehensive). Note this is electronic filing/direct-debit payment integrated with tax and customs administration rather than confirmed integration specifically with an instant/real-time payment rail.
revised_comments: Morocco's Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) operates the SIMPL online portal (tax.gov.ma), through which electronic filing and payment of Corporate Tax, VAT and Personal Income Tax has been mandatory for all taxpayers since January 2017. Separately, the customs authority (ADII) operates the BADR electronic customs clearance system, which supports electronic payment of customs duties and taxes. Together these cover the main state taxes and customs revenue through digital payment channels.

The overarching legal texts are publicly accessible, though a scheme-specific rulebook for participants is not confirmed to be independently published online.

Comments: Independent audits/reviews for payment system operators were not evidenced with publicly available audit reports in this run. revision_notes: Escalated from fast-path Unknown. Bank Al-Maghrib's 2023 annual report on financial market infrastructure confirms that Financial Market Infrastructures (IMFs, including SIMT/GSIMT) undergo external audits against the CROE (Cyber Resilience Oversight Expectations) framework — by end-2023, 2 of 5 IMFs had completed external audits showing 'excellent' coverage of required measures, with the remainder in progress. Decree n°2-21-406 (cybersecurity law) additionally mandates external audit of sensitive information systems for critical infrastructure operators. This is distinct from the previously-cited BAM statutory audit of its own accounts, which does not evidence payment-system-operator audits. Audit conduct is confirmed and summarised in a public annual report, but full audit reports are not published. Score revised from 0/Unknown to 2 (audits conducted; disclosure limited to summary commentary rather than full findings). Flagged for human review given the summarised, non-itemised nature of the public disclosure.
revised_comments: Morocco's financial market infrastructures, including the interbank payment clearing system, are subject to periodic external cybersecurity audits under Bank Al-Maghrib's CROE (Cyber Resilience Oversight Expectations) framework and the national cybersecurity decree (n°2-21-406), which requires external audit of sensitive information systems for critical infrastructure operators. Bank Al-Maghrib's annual report on financial market infrastructure summarises audit progress and findings, though detailed audit reports themselves are not made public.

In March 2023, the Professional Grouping of Banks in Morocco (GPBM), under Bank Al-Maghrib's aegis, adopted an inter-banking charter committing member banks to improve physical (branches, ATMs) and digital-interface accessibility for persons with disabilities, developed in consultation with disability associations. Morocco's National Financial Inclusion Strategy (SNIF) report separately documents a benchmarking exercise on international best practice in disability-inclusive financial services (including reference to WCAG web-accessibility guidelines) and an action plan targeting Morocco's roughly 3 million adults with disabilities. This is a sector-wide commitment/framework with concrete but not yet verified nationwide implementation, so the score is revised from 0/Unknown to 2/Partial.
revised_comments: Morocco's banking sector has adopted an inter-banking charter (2023), overseen by Bank Al-Maghrib, committing banks to improve the accessibility of branches, ATMs and digital interfaces for persons with disabilities. This follows a National Financial Inclusion Strategy benchmarking exercise on disability-inclusive design, including reference to web-accessibility (WCAG) guidelines, targeting the roughly 3 million Moroccan adults living with a disability. Implementation is at an early, commitment-based stage rather than confirmed comprehensive accessible coverage.
